results.title: Top 10 Bioinformatics Breakthroughs of 2022! - CBIRT
results.content: Simulation of a Living Cell Enabled with NVIDIA GPUs. The prayers for a computerized model of a cell, the fundamental unit of life, to predict its biology and uncover new ones were answered through a study conducted predominantly by scientists at the University of Illinois. Scientists from the Center for Advanced Bioenergy and Bioproducts Innovation developed the first ever open-source software, CROPSR, that can predict and evaluate guide RNA sequences from the organism’s genome. In an effort to level the playing ground and provide even small data centers equal opportunity in scientific discovery, the researchers at John Hopkins University developed a cloud-based platform, AnVIL (Genomic Data Science Analysis, Visualization, and Informatics Lab-space). On top of being one of the largest genomic databases with sequences from over 300,000 genomes, Anvil also provides resources for data analysis. Through machine learning and omics data, the scientists at the University of Texas developed the platform REFLECT (REcurrent Features LEveraged for Combination Therapy) that recommends drug combinations tailored for the molecular characteristics of the tumor.

results.title: Funded Research - Wharton AI & Analytics Initiative
results.content: Recently, Wharton AI and Analytics Initiative funded a project to study “Reducing Gender and Racial Disparities in the Use of Generative AI in the Workplace.” While this research intends to enhance both academic research and practice over the longer-term, there is an immediate need to ensure that the “digital divide” in AI adoption does not manifest (or widen) among students enrolled in the courses, MGMT 2240 and MGMT 6240, Leading Diversity in Organizations. This research project aims to investigate the impact of artificial intelligence (AI) investments by non-tech firms (AI-adopters) on product market competition, innovation, and industry dynamics. With proprietary data from Upwork Inc., the researchers are able to access full information on a large sample of jobs and workers over time, thus obtaining findings that can inform the effects of generative AI on the labor market and careers.
